statement: For every positive integer n, (19^(n/3)-1)/(2n) <= g_4(n) <= 8*19^(ceil(n/3)-1), hence lim_{n->infinity} g_4(n)^(1/n)=19^(1/3).
Every [-2,2]-coefficient relation over a four-AP-free subset-sum set splits into separately vanishing magnitude-one and magnitude-two layers.
Minimal signed relations have pairwise disjoint supports up to sign, and every signed relation decomposes uniquely over those blocks.
The entire coefficient box kernel [-2,2]^n is the product of scalar kernels on the disjoint minimal signed-relation blocks.
|T(A)|=3^t product_j (3^(m_j)-2^(m_j)) for the ternary-sum image and the disjoint block decomposition.
For u,v,w in {-2,-1,0,1,2}, 19 divides u+7v+8w iff (u,v,w)=t(1,1,-1).
D={0,1,7,8,9,15,16} contains no nonconstant four-term progression modulo 19.
For every m>=1, the subset-sum set of union_{j=0}^{m-1} 19^j{1,7,8} contains no nonconstant integer four-term arithmetic progression.

For every natural number n>0 there exists B:Finset Z with B.card=n, every b in B satisfying 1<=b<=8*19^((n+2)/3-1), and FourAPFree(subsetSums B), where division and subtraction in the exponent are natural-number operations and subsetSums includes the empty sum.
Distinctness sharpens the finite lower bound to g_4(n)>=ceil((19^(n/3)+n(n-1)-1)/(2n)).
This work does not address the separate k=3 question (answered negatively by Costa 2026), all of Erdős Problem 817, or establish novelty or priority.
